gaps.sentence: They're ___ up a new office in the old warehouse district.
The caterpillar will turn ___ a butterfly.
Everyone says she takes ___ her grandmother.
gaps.explanation: take after a relative = resemble them in character/looks.

gaps.sentence: She ___ down an offer from a rival university.
The protesters set ___ at dawn from the village square.
gaps.explanation: set off/out = begin a journey; set up = establish.

gaps.sentence: I ran ___ my old teacher at the airport.
gaps.explanation: run into somebody = meet them by chance (also: bump into).

gaps.sentence: She waited at the restaurant for an hour, but he had stood her ___ again.
gaps.explanation: 'Stand somebody up' = fail to keep an arranged meeting.

gaps.sentence: The concert tickets sold ___ within an hour.
gaps.explanation: sell out = all tickets/goods are sold.
